messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Continuous-batching anomaly detected - KV cache growth (node-group A) + elevated batch token sizes. Rule: cont-batch.max_batch_tokens > threshold. Metric: kv_cache_entries_total x5 baseline.

maria: seeing 5xx rate up ~3x for /v1/generate for customers pinned to v1-large on us-west-2.

jordan: looking at the runtime flags we rolled two hours ago — did we change max_batch_tokens or max_num_seqs?

sam: yes, we bumped default max_batch_tokens from 4096 -> 16384 to optimize throughput for long-context tests. that was in canary but accidentally merged to prod config.

priya: that explains KV cache blowup. more tokens per batch -> larger KV caches kept across sequences -> memory churn.

leo: logs from node-12: "kv_cache_evictions=0, kv_cache_items=6.2M, batch_tokens=14k". dump attached in thread.

maria: customer impact list incoming. Support bot: any active tickets?

support-bot: Ticket #4521 (ACME Corp) - slow responses, median latency 1.8s -> 8s, reported at 2024-11-03T18:22Z. Another ticket #4522 (BetaApps) - sporadic 504s.

jordan: initial mitigation: short-term config override to reduce max_batch_tokens to 4096 on us-west-2 node-group A. I'll run the override now.

ops-runner: running command:
```bash
redwoodctl runtime override set --scope=us-west-2 --pool=node-group-A --key=cont_batch.max_batch_tokens --value=4096
```

ops-runner: override applied. propagating. expect ~30s to reach workers.

maria: rolling restart of affected pool to free huge kv caches? or wait for eviction?

priya: prefer soft approach: throttle new long batches, set batching timeout low so small requests don't accumulate. set cont_batch.max_batch_timeout_ms=25 for this pool.

ops-runner: applying timeout change:
```bash
redwoodctl runtime override set --scope=us-west-2 --pool=node-group-A --key=cont_batch.max_batch_timeout_ms --value=25
```

ops-runner: timeout change applied.

sam: still seeing high memory on a subset of hosts, last GC didn't free huge KV segments. I'm going to cordon node-10 and restart it gracefully.

jordan: ack. cordon + drain node-10.

ops-runner: cordon/drain commands:
```bash
kube drain node-10 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kube uncordon node-10
```

leo: node-10 drained and restarted. KV cache entries dropped from 6.2M -> 120k on restart.

maria: metrics trending down after overrides + node restart. 5xx rate back to baseline in last 3m.

support-bot: sent updates to customers: ACME ticket #4521 status -> mitigated, recommending they clear any client-side retries.

jordan: root cause summary for P0: accidental prod rollout of canary change increasing cont_batch.max_batch_tokens to 16384. This increased per-batch token aggregation, leading to oversized KV cache retention and memory pressure -> tails of latency and some OOMs causing 502/504s.

priya: immediate action items captured:
- revert prod default to 4096 (done via override)
- add automated guard: alert when avg_batch_tokens > 6k per node for 5m
- add pre-merge test that verifies runtime overrides don't accidentally promote canary to prod
- schedule capacity-aware rollout for any future increases

sam: deploying a hotfix to make overrides explicit and gated. PR 2387 in review.

maria: handing off to night oncall @jordan. i'm stepping out in 10m but will stay reachable if anything regresses.

jordan: taking over. I'll monitor the next 2 hours and coordinate customer communications.

ops-runner: posting post-mortem checklist to /incidents/postmortems. please add timelines and links to dashboards.

leo: quick note: discovered a related config key cont_batch.max_num_seqs was set at 256 in the canary patch. that allowed more sequences per batch offload. lowering to 64 by default in next rollout.

priya: agreed. final permanent fix: default max_batch_tokens=4096, max_num_seqs=64, timeout_ms=30. also add an automated rollback if node memory > 85% for 3m.

jordan: recording final status: mitigated at 2024-11-03T19:10Z. customer impact limited to a small subset of customers (2-5) with long-context workloads. No data loss. Follow-up: postmortem and action items due EOD.

maria: thanks team. :thumbsup: we'll do a blameless postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: cont-batch config regression. Severity: Sev2 -> downgraded after mitigation. All alerts cleared."
